adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the approved 1962 Benziger printing sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Ordo Missae of Pallottinum, Poznań 1963, which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
The selected accentuation and punctuation follow the edition. The pinned digital reading is recorded exactly; the word is the same.
The selected spelling follows the edition. The pinned digital spelling and any accompanying punctuation are recorded exactly; both readings represent the same word.
The approved Benziger printing's spelling is retained under the house orthography. The witness reading is the same word in another editorial spelling.

The approved Benziger printing prints this numeral as one word, nonagintanóvem, across a line end (p. 375), where it prints the same numeral as two words earlier on the page. The edition prints two words in both places, as the Vulgate and the digital source do.
